questions.stem: Dolly the sheep was produced by somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT). The nucleus from an udder cell of Sheep A was inserted into an enucleated egg cell from Sheep B, and the embryo was implanted into Sheep C. Which sheep is Dolly genetically identical to?

options.text: Sheep B, because the egg cell came from her
Sheep C, because she carried the pregnancy
Sheep A, because the nuclear DNA came from her body cell
A combination of all three sheep

questions.explanation: Dolly's nuclear DNA (which contains the vast majority of genetic information) came from the udder cell of Sheep A. The egg cell from Sheep B was enucleated (had its nucleus removed), so it contributed only a tiny amount of mitochondrial DNA. Sheep C was the surrogate mother and contributed no genetic material. Dolly was a genetic clone of Sheep A.

questions.stem: A gardener takes cuttings from a rose plant with particularly large, fragrant flowers and grows them into new plants. Why is this method of cloning useful?

options.text: It produces plants with greater genetic variation than the parent
It guarantees all new plants will have the same desirable characteristics as the parent, since they are genetically identical
It is the only way to reproduce rose plants
The new plants will be more resistant to disease than the parent

questions.explanation: Taking cuttings produces clones - genetically identical copies of the parent plant. This means all new plants will share the parent's desirable characteristics (large, fragrant flowers). This is faster than growing from seed and guarantees the phenotype. The disadvantage is that all clones share the same disease susceptibility due to their identical genotypes.

questions.stem: Tissue culture is used to clone plants in large numbers. Small groups of cells are taken from a plant and grown in sterile nutrient medium. Why must the conditions be sterile?

options.text: Sterile conditions make the plants grow faster
Small plant cell groups have no immune system; bacteria or fungi in non-sterile conditions would outcompete and kill the plant cells
Sterile conditions increase genetic variation in the clones
Sterile conditions are only needed for the first day of growth

questions.explanation: Plant tissue culture starts with tiny groups of undifferentiated cells that are extremely vulnerable to microbial contamination. The nutrient-rich growth medium that feeds the plant cells would also be an ideal environment for bacteria and fungi to grow. These microorganisms would quickly outcompete and destroy the delicate plant cells. Sterile conditions prevent contamination.

questions.stem: Some people argue that cloning endangered animals could help save species from extinction. Which is a valid scientific limitation of this approach?

options.text: Cloned animals would be a different species from the original
Cloning produces genetically identical individuals, so the population would lack genetic diversity needed to adapt to environmental changes and resist disease
Cloned animals cannot reproduce
Cloning technology only works with sheep

questions.explanation: While cloning could increase the number of individuals of an endangered species, all clones would be genetically identical (or nearly so). A population lacking genetic diversity is vulnerable to being wiped out by a single disease or environmental change. Long-term species survival requires genetic variation for adaptation through natural selection. Cloning addresses numbers but not diversity.

questions.stem: Embryo splitting is a technique where an early embryo is divided into two halves, each of which develops into a separate organism. How does this differ from adult cell cloning (SCNT)?

options.text: Embryo splitting produces non-identical offspring, while SCNT produces identical ones
Embryo splitting divides a naturally formed embryo to produce identical twins; SCNT creates an embryo from a body cell nucleus and is a clone of an existing adult
SCNT is simpler and more reliable than embryo splitting
Embryo splitting requires genetic engineering, while SCNT does not

questions.explanation: In embryo splitting, an embryo produced by normal fertilisation is divided at an early stage, producing genetically identical twins. In SCNT, the nucleus from an adult body cell is transferred into an enucleated egg cell, creating an embryo that is a clone of the adult cell donor. Embryo splitting copies an embryo; SCNT copies an existing adult organism.
